extracted.intended_audience: users/developers of the SINGULAR computer algebra system (mathematicians/researchers using SINGULAR libraries)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for SINGULAR library procedures (usage, assumptions, return values, and examples) across multiple libraries (classifyMapGerms.lib, combinat.lib, curveInv.lib, deRham.lib, divisors.lib). Intended to guide correct invocation and interpretation of outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: classifySimpleMaps
rubrics_metrics.description: classifySimpleMaps(I); I = an ideal with 2 generators in a polynomial ring with 2 variables and local ordering defining a map germ C^2 to C^2. Compute the normal form of the germ in Rieger's classification if it is simple.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: normal form of I, of type ideal. Note: If I is not simple it returns (0,0). Example invocation shown with LIB "classifyMapGerms.lib"; constructing ring, polynomials, map and calling classifySimpleMaps(I) which returns the normal form (example output: x and xy+y5+y7).

rubrics_metrics.name: classifySimpleMaps1
rubrics_metrics.description: classifySimpleMaps1(I); same input type as classifySimpleMaps (ideal with 2 generators in a polynomial ring with 2 variables defining a map germ C^2 to C^2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute: the normal form of the germ in Rieger's classification if it is simple. Return: normal form of I, of type ideal. Note: If I is not simple it returns (0,0). Example usage mirrors classifySimpleMaps with same example output.

rubrics_metrics.name: classifyUnimodalMaps
rubrics_metrics.description: classifyUnimodalMaps(I); I an ideal with 2 generators in a polynomial ring with 2 variables and local ordering defining a map germ C^2 to C^2. Compute the normal form of the germ in Rieger's classification if it is unimodal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: normal form of I, of type ideal. Note: If I is not unimodal it returns (0,0). Example provided using LIB "classifyMapGerms.lib" and polynomials f1=x, f2=xy+y6+y9 yielding output x and xy+y6+y9.

rubrics_metrics.name: intersectLists
rubrics_metrics.description: intersectLists(L,M); L list, M list. Return a list containing all elements of L which are elements of M.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theory: requires elements of lists to have a compare operator ==. Examples: intersectLists(list(1,1,2,2,3),list(2,3,3,4)) returns [2,3]; intersectLists(list(1,1,2,2,3),list(1,1,2,2,3)) returns [1,2,3].

rubrics_metrics.name: sublists
rubrics_metrics.description: sublists(L); L list. Return the list of all sublists of L.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: L is a list. Example demonstrates enumerating all sublists of list(1,2,3,4,5) with many outputs printed; behavior illustrated by concrete outputs for small indices.

rubrics_metrics.name: member
rubrics_metrics.description: member(e,L); e element, L list. Return 1 if e is an element of L, 0 otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theory: requires elements involved to have a compare operator ==. Example: member(1,list(1,4,5)) returns 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: curveDeltaInv
rubrics_metrics.description: curveDeltaInv(I); I ideal. Assume I is a radical ideal, dim(R/I) = 1. Return the delta invariant of R/I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes: Output -1 means the delta invariant is infinite. Optional parameter: if normalization already computed, pass list L containing output of normal (with options prim, wd and usering for mixed ordering) as second argument: curveDeltaInv(I,L). Examples: finite case returns 9, infinite case (ideal xyz) returns -1. See also curveConductorMult and other curveInv procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: curveConductorMult
rubrics_metrics.description: curveConductorMult(I); I ideal. Assume I is a radical ideal, dim(R/I) = 1. Return the multiplicity of the conductor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optional parameter: can supply normalization output (normal(...)) as second argument. Examples show computing conductor multiplicity after standardization std(radical(I)). For Gorenstein curve, note c = 2*delta; example: for ideal xy, delta=1 and curveConductorMult returns 2. References: Section D.4.18.15 [normalConductor].

rubrics_metrics.name: curveDeligneNumber
rubrics_metrics.description: curveDeligneNumber(I); I ideal. Assume I is a radical ideal, dim(R/I) = 1. Return the Deligne number e of R/I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remarks: By definition e = 3*delta - m, so algorithm computes delta invariant and colength of derivations m. Optional parameter: can use normalization output list L from normal(...). Examples: shows several rings/ideals and outputs (30, 5, 15). Also demonstrates comparing Milnor number to Deligne number and using Saito's criterion. See also curveColengthDerivations and curveDeltaInv.

rubrics_metrics.name: curveColengthDerivations
rubrics_metrics.description: curveColengthDerivations(I); I ideal. Assume I is a radical ideal. Return the colength of derivations of R/I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remarks: procedure computes colength branchwise and sums; optional parameter: normalization output list L may be supplied. Examples: returns values for several example ideals (9,4,15).

rubrics_metrics.name: deRhamCohomology
rubrics_metrics.description: deRhamCohomology(L[,choices]); L a list of polynomials, choices an optional list of up to three strings controlling algorithms. Computes de Rham cohomology of the complement of the affine variety given by polynomials in L.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optional strings: one of {'noCE','Vdres','Sres'} (control Cartan-Eilenberg resolution usage), one of {'iterativeloc','no iterativeloc'} (localization strategy), and one of {'onlybounds','exactroots'} (bounds vs exact integer roots of global b-function). Defaults: 'noCE', 'iterativeloc', 'onlybounds'. Assume: basering must be a polynomial ring over Q. Return: list where ith entry is (i-1)st de Rham cohomology group of complement. Example: for L=(xy,xz) returns list [1,1,0,1,1]. References provided in header (Oaku & Takayama, Walther, Rottner).

rubrics_metrics.name: MVComplex
rubrics_metrics.description: MVComplex(L); L a list of polynomials. Compute the Mayer–Vietoris/Mayer–Vietoris-type complex representing the complex used for de Rham computations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: basering is polynomial ring with n variables and rational coefficients; L is list of non-constant polynomials. Return: ring W (nth Weyl algebra) containing list MV representing the Mayer–Vietoris complex (C^i,d^i) with specified structure: C^i given by D^n^ncols(...) / im(...), differentials by entries C[2*i]. Example demonstrates def C=MVComplex(L); setring C; MV; and prints matrices/entries representing complex.

rubrics_metrics.name: makeDivisor
rubrics_metrics.description: makeDivisor(I,J); I = ideal, J = ideal. Construct a divisor on a qring Q of a smooth irreducible variety X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: I and J are ideals in a qring Q of a smooth irreducible variety X such that any ideal in Q satisfies S2 condition. Return: a divisor on X. Theory: procedure eliminates all components not of codimension 1; S2 condition required so every proper nonzero principal ideal has pure codimension 1. Example shows creating qring Q = std(I) and divisor P = makeDivisor(ideal(x,z),ideal(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: divisorplus
rubrics_metrics.description: divisorplus(A,B); compute A + B where A and B are divisors on X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: A and B are divisors on X. Return: a divisor on X. Theory: computes product of numerator ideals and product of denominator ideals respectively. Example shows A+B -> printed representation like (x,yz) - (1).

rubrics_metrics.name: multdivisor
rubrics_metrics.description: multdivisor(n,A); multiply divisor A by integer n (A*n).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: n integer, A divisor on X. Return: divisor on X. Theory: computes nth power of numerator and denominator ideals. Examples: multdivisor(4,A) and A*4 produce (z2,xz) - (1).

rubrics_metrics.name: negativedivisor
rubrics_metrics.description: negativedivisor(A); return A*(-1) (the negative of a divisor).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: A is a divisor on X. Return: a divisor on X. Theory: interchanges numerator and denominator ideals. Example: A = (z,x) - (1) gives negativedivisor(A) = (1) - (z,x).

rubrics_metrics.name: normalForm (divisors)
rubrics_metrics.description: normalForm(A); A = divisor. Return a different representative of the same divisor on X by cancelling common components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: A is a divisor on X. Return: normalized divisor. Theory: cancels common components of numerator and denominator. Example: constructing D = (A+B)+multdivisor(-1,B) prints (x,yz) - (y,x); normalForm(D) returns (z,x) - (1).

rubrics_metrics.name: isEqualDivisor
rubrics_metrics.description: isEqualDivisor(A,B); check equality of two divisors A and B on X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: A and B are divisors on X. Return: int 0 or 1. Theory: computes normal forms of A and B and compares. Example: isEqualDivisor(A,D) returns 1 after creating D as combination of A and B.

rubrics_metrics.name: globalSections
rubrics_metrics.description: globalSections(A); A = divisor. Return a list with a basis of the space of global sections of A (the divisor).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: qring of X satisfies S2-condition and X is smooth. Theory: compute sat((f*J) : I) / f where D = (I)-(J). Example: globalSections(D) returned a list with monomials [x2, z2, yz, xz] for a given divisor D (printed as entries).

rubrics_metrics.name: degreeDivisor
rubrics_metrics.description: degreeDivisor(A); A = divisor. Return the degree of A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: A is a divisor on X. Theory: compute difference of degrees of numerator and denominator ideals. Example: degreeDivisor(P) returned 1 for P = makeDivisor(ideal(x,z),ideal(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: linearlyEquivalent
rubrics_metrics.description: linearlyEquivalent(A,B); test whether divisors A and B are linearly equivalent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: A and B are divisors on X. Return: list L=(f,g) if A and B are linearly equivalent (A-B = (f/g)), or int 0 otherwise. Theory: checks whether A-B is principal. Example: linearlyEquivalent(A,B) returned 0; linearlyEquivalent(multdivisor(2,A),multdivisor(2,B)) returned [x, z].

rubrics_metrics.name: effective (eﬀective)
rubrics_metrics.description: effective(A); A = divisor. When A is linearly equivalent to an effective divisor, return that effective divisor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: A is a divisor on X which is linearly equivalent to an effective divisor. Return: divisor on X. (Page text cuts off mid-description but usage header and intent are clear: produce an effective representative when one exists.)
